title: Emergency Pressure Relief System
model_title: Emergency Pressure Relief System — Twin PSVs on a Change-over Valve, Rupture Disc & Relief Header

introduction.definition: An emergency pressure relief system protects equipment from overpressure. Spring-loaded safety valves (PSVs), often duplicated on an interlocked change-over valve, and/or a rupture disc open automatically at the set pressure and discharge into a closed relief header that drains to the flare knockout drum.
applications: Pressure vessels, columns, exchangers and reactors in process plants
Compressors, pumps (thermal relief) and storage systems
key_points: Last line of defence (not a control device)
Inlet loss < 3 %, back pressure within limits

pressure.title: Relieve before the vessel is overstressed
pressure.description: Every pressure vessel needs relief for its credible overpressure scenarios (blocked outlet, fire, control-valve failure, runaway reaction). A PSV is set at or below the MAWP and sized for the worst relieving rate; allowable accumulation is typically 10 % (single valve), 16 % (multiple) or 21 % (fire case) above MAWP (ASME VIII / API 520 — verify edition). Inlet pressure loss should stay below ≈ 3 % of set pressure to avoid chatter. The change-over valve allows testing a spare without losing protection.

script.narration: This module introduces the Emergency Pressure Relief System.
An emergency pressure relief system protects equipment from overpressure.

Spring-loaded safety valves (PSVs), often duplicated on an interlocked change-over valve, and/or a rupture disc open automatically at the set pressure and discharge into a closed relief header that drains to the flare knockout drum.
Typical applications include pressure vessels, columns, exchangers and reactors in process plants; compressors, pumps (thermal relief) and storage systems.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Emergency Pressure Relief System works.
A fire or upset raises vessel pressure.
The PSV disc lifts at set pressure.
Gas flows into the relief header.
The change-over valve keeps one PSV always in service.
The rupture disc gives fast full-bore relief if needed.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Every pressure vessel needs relief for its credible overpressure scenarios (blocked outlet, fire, control-valve failure, runaway reaction).

video_tutorials.title: Emergency Pressure Relief System — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Emergency Pressure Relief System.
Check car-seals / change-over position.
Bench-test PSVs per interval (RBI).
Overhaul PSVs; replace rupture discs per schedule.
Watch for PSV chatter: rapid opening/closing, damage. Common cause: high inlet loss, oversizing.
Watch for stuck closed: no relief at set. Common cause: fouling, corrosion.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
